title: Black Light FTL Route Safety Integration Registry
purpose: Bridge the existing EXO FTL route environment generator to versioned safety calibration and certification without promoting gameplay-normalized route packets into setting canon.

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Family-specific gravity/miscalculation behavior, safety lookahead, emergency de-transit, increasing maturity margins, and non-perfect safety.

authority.statusRule: Route archetype packets are PROPOSED simulation mappings unless a named source explicitly provides measured environmental values.

deep-space.notes: Clean comparison environment; still not hazard-free.

planetary-well.notes: Represents the existing planetary-well route penalty in normalized safety space, not a universal planetary constant.

gas-giant.notes: Adds magnetic/plasma observability burden to gravity-driven difficulty.

binary.notes: Time-varying competing gradients are emphasized over raw potential.

compact-object.notes: Intended to drive frequent rejection rather than normalize compact-object proximity as routine transit.

nebula.notes: Sensor/model uncertainty dominates over gravity severity.

uncharted.notes: Unknown mass and model incompleteness are intentionally the primary hazard channels.

q-disturbed.notes: Higher-dimensional boundary/model uncertainty dominates the route.

integrationRules: The adapter must preserve the generated family and must never use certification to auto-select a different family.
Route archetype values are PROPOSED normalized simulation inputs, not measured astrophysical constants.
Calibration profile identity/version must be copied into every generated route safety result.
REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, and CONFLICT states must survive into presentation and export.
A generated speed/range value is capability modeling, not proof that the selected route is certified safe.
Family-specific required hazards are additive to route hazards.
Higher maturity may improve lookahead, covariance, redundancy, and recovery margins but cannot suppress a governing hard hazard.
Named-source unresolved overrides remain unresolved and may not inherit the generic family baseline as named canon.
canonGuards: Do not describe PROPOSED route archetype numbers as real astrophysical measurements.
Do not convert route difficulty into a universal FTL constant.
Do not certify a route when calibration is unresolved or conflicting.
Do not hide REJECTED or UNRESOLVED behind a generated performance number.
Do not infer a named civilization or installation limit from the generic simulation baseline.
Do not turn a selected UI family into evidence for an unresolved archaeological family.
Do not claim perfect safety at any path maturity.
Do not spend protected recovery reserve to improve nominal advertised performance.
